title: Coefficient compatibility of ordered affine-space adjunctions
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$, and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and choose $N=\ell^n\geq1$ annihilating both. On small ordinary etale sites use constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and $T_T=(-)_B=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Write $D^b_{ctf}$ for bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude, as in [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer], and $R_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$ for $R=A,B$ [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. Let $p_d:\mathbf A^d_S\to S$ for a standing base $S$ and $d\geq0$. Use the ordered affine-space adjunction of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], namely the composite of open affine-line extension and normalized projective-line adjunctions, with right functor $G_{d,R}=p_d^*(-)(d)[2d]$ and actual counit $\epsilon_{d,R}$. Identify its left functor with $F_{d,R}=Rp_{d!,R}$ on bounded-below inputs using [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. Let $\beta_d:T_SF_{d,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{d,B}T_{\mathbf A^d_S}$ be the coefficient map for any fixed compactification [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility], and let $a_{d,K}:T_{\mathbf A^d_S}G_{d,A}K\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{d,B}T_SK$ be the canonical tensor/pullback, twist and shift comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(S_{et},A)$,
$$\epsilon_{d,B,T_SK}\,F_{d,B}(a_{d,K})\,\beta_d(G_{d,A}K)=T_S(\epsilon_{d,A,K}).$$
For $d=0$ this is the identity adjunction. The equation uses the coefficient map for the specified compactification, not merely an unspecified isomorphism between its endpoints.

source.place: Charts: iterated projective-line integration over the ordered coordinate tower; retained Steps 9 and 10

proof.text: Use the coordinate tower $X_0=S$, $X_{r+1}=\mathbf A^1_{X_r}$, $u_r:X_{r+1}\to X_r$, $p_{r+1}=p_ru_r$, and its standard compactifications $j_r:X_{r+1}\hookrightarrow P_r=\mathbf P^1_{X_r}$, $q_r:P_r\to X_r$ of [def-amb-affine-trace-tower]. All these schemes and maps are in the standing setting: affine and projective spaces and their standard open charts over a separated finite-type $k$-scheme remain separated and finite type. The integer $N$ is invertible since $\ell\ne p$. By [lem-sp-etale-ctf-chart-domain], every coefficient extension and every pullback followed by a finite positive Tate twist and shift used below preserves $D^b_{ctf}$; the compact-support functors also preserve it. Consequently each successive right-adjoint input, not just the original $K$, lies in the domains of the two scalar-counit lemmas below. In particular all inputs to bounded-below compact-support comparisons and their coefficient extensions are bounded below. No assertion that tensoring with $B$ preserves all of $D^+$ is needed.

source.place: Charts: domains of the ordered coordinate tower

proof.text: Fix one stage with base $T=X_r$. Write $J_R=Dj_!$, $H_R=j^*$, $Q_R=Rq_{*,R}$, $V_R=q^*(-)(1)[2]$, with counits $v_R:J_RH_R\to1$ and $w_R:Q_RV_R\to1$. For an open immersion the sum extension is the usual extension by zero, by [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension]. Apply [lem-sp-etale-sum-counit-scalar] to $j$ and [lem-sp-p1-counit-scalar] to $q$. If $s:T_PJ_A\xrightarrow{\sim}J_BT_{\mathbf A^1_T}$ and $b:T_TQ_A\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_BT_P$ are their specified coefficient maps, the canonical right comparisons $h:T_{\mathbf A^1_T}H_A\xrightarrow{\sim}H_BT_P$ and $a:T_PV_A\xrightarrow{\sim}V_BT_T$ are respectively the mates of $s^{-1}$ and $b^{-1}$. These statements concern the actual evaluation and normalized projective-line counits, at every finite-Tor input; no replacement of either adjunction by an arbitrary isomorphic one is made.

source.place: Charts: open evaluation and normalized projective-line counits

proof.text:
Compose $J_R\dashv H_R$ with $Q_R\dashv V_R$. Its left functor is $L_R=Q_RJ_R$, its right functor is $W_R=H_RV_R$, and its counit is $e_R=w_R\circ Q_R(v_RV_R)$ by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Put $b^u=Q_B(s)\circ bJ_A$ and $a^u=H_B(a)\circ hV_A$. Apply clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] to the inverse squares $s^{-1}$ and $b^{-1}$. Their pasted square is $(b^u)^{-1}$, and its mate is exactly $a^u$. The transpose characterization in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] therefore gives
$$e_{B,T_TK}\circ L_B(a^u_K)\circ b^u(W_AK)=T_T(e_{A,K}).$$
This is the scalar-counit equation for the standard affine-line compactification. The left map here is the proper coefficient comparison followed by open extension's tensor comparison, exactly the chosen-compactification definition of the coefficient map in [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility].

source.place: Charts: compose the open and projective-line scalar squares

proof.text: Under the ordered right-functor normal forms of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], the pasted right comparisons are the canonical pullback/tensor, Tate and shift comparisons in the question. Here is the normalization check. Inverse image takes each Tate factor to the same factor upstairs, compatibly with tensor and composition, by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Use the K-flat, flat-term representatives and the natural tensor/pullback isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Tate factors are flat by [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line], so they require no further derived replacements. On each local generator of the Tate factors every order of the displayed coefficient reassociations sends $((x\otimes z_1\otimes\cdots\otimes z_r)\otimes b)$ to $(x\otimes b)\otimes\bar z_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\bar z_r$, where $\bar z_i=z_i\otimes1$. Both parenthesizations multiply coefficients by the same balanced rule $(x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes\varphi(a)b$. Thus the maps agree termwise and hence after descent to the derived category. Shifts commute with this degree-zero map; all accumulated shifts are even, so their reassociations introduce no extra sign. For one coordinate this identifies $a^u$ with the named affine-line comparison.

source.place: Charts: identify the pasted right square with the canonical tensor map

proof.text:
Induct on $r$ before identifying the left functor with a compactification. Let $\mathcal F_{r,R}$ be the ordered composite of the line functors above and $\mathcal G_{r,R}$ its reverse ordered right composite. Let $B_r:T_S\mathcal F_{r,A}\to\mathcal F_{r,B}T_{X_r}$ be the ordered composite of the $b^u$ and $A_r:T_{X_r}\mathcal G_{r,A}\to\mathcal G_{r,B}T_S$ the ordered composite of the $a^u$. The induction claim is that $A_r$ is the mate of $B_r^{-1}$ and
$$\mathcal E_{r,B}\,\mathcal F_{r,B}(A_r)\,B_r\mathcal G_{r,A}=T_S(\mathcal E_{r,A}),$$
where $\mathcal E_r$ is the actual composite counit. For $r=0$, both functors, both comparisons, and the counit are identities. The identity-adjunction formula of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] proves the claim, and it includes $K=0$ and the empty base.

source.place: Charts: induction claim and identity base case

proof.text:
For the successor, $\mathcal F_{r+1,R}=\mathcal F_{r,R}L_{u_r,R}$ and $\mathcal G_{r+1,R}=W_{u_r,R}\mathcal G_{r,R}$. The ordered comparisons are
$$B_{r+1}=\mathcal F_{r,B}(b^{u_r})\circ B_rL_{u_r,A},\qquad A_{r+1}=W_{u_r,B}(A_r)\circ a^{u_r}\mathcal G_{r,A}.$$
By the induction hypothesis and the affine-line calculation in step 3, clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] says exactly that $A_{r+1}$ is the mate of $B_{r+1}^{-1}$. Its transpose equation [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] is the induction claim in degree $r+1$. The actual counit used here is $\mathcal E_{r+1,R}=\mathcal E_{r,R}\circ\mathcal F_{r,R}(e_{u_r,R}\mathcal G_{r,R})$, as prescribed by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Hence the calculation tracks the specified counit at every step. Step 4 identifies $A_{r+1}$ with the canonical $a_{r+1}$ after the right normal form, not merely with some isomorphism of its endpoints. Induction proves the equation in every dimension.

source.place: Charts: successor step for the ordered coordinate tower

proof.text:
Fix the compactification $c$ specified in the question and write $C_{d,R}:\mathcal F_{d,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}F^c_{d,R}$ for its comparison with the ordered composite. These are the canonical coherent composition/refinement maps of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. The composition and refinement equalities of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility], applied successively, give on our input class
$$\beta_d\circ T_S(C_{d,A})=(C_{d,B}T_{X_d})\circ B_d.$$
The identity/composition normalization gives this also for $d=0$. This step uses the refinement equality as well as the composition equality: if $c$ differs from the compactification used to form a composition map, the common-refinement comparison contributes precisely $C_{d,R}$ on both sides. Thus $\beta_d$ is the coefficient map for $c$ itself. Domain preservation in step 1 ensures that every equality is applied to the bounded finite-Tor inputs stipulated in its statement.

source.place: Charts: pass the ordered left comparison to the fixed compactification

proof.text:
After the right normal-form identification, the counit on $F^c_{d,R}$ is $\epsilon_{d,R}=\mathcal E_{d,R}\circ C_{d,R}(G_{d,R})^{-1}$, by the prescribed identification in [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. Precompose the desired equation with the isomorphism $T_S(C_{d,A}(G_{d,A}K))$. Substitute the equality in step 7 and then naturality of $C_{d,B}$ at $a_{d,K}$; its left side becomes
$$\mathcal E_{d,B,T_SK}\,\mathcal F_{d,B}(a_{d,K})\,B_d(G_{d,A}K).$$
By steps 5--6 this equals $T_S(\mathcal E_{d,A,K})$, which is also the right side after that precomposition. Cancel the isomorphism. This proves exactly the stated equality for $\beta_d^c$, including the identity adjunction in dimension zero. The proof never assumes flatness or finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$; coefficient tensor products throughout are derived.

source.place: Charts: cancel the specified compactification comparisons

This is a first split with no new nodes; the statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to Q36's version, proof_deps equals the union of step uses, there is no cycle and no SGA source. Step 1: lem-sp-etale-ctf-chart-domain shows J=Dj_!, H=j^* (a=0), Q=Rq_*, V=q^*(1)[2] and T all preserve D^b_ctf, so the adjunctions restrict to those subcategories. Step 2: the sum/evaluation counit of lem-sp-etale-sum-counit-scalar for the open immersion j is the recollement counit of j_!⊣j^* (one summand), which is also how lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization identifies them. The p1 lemma uses the same t_q normalization as def-amb-p1-trace. Mate orientation checked: the mate of β^{-1} is a. Step 3: mate-pasting clause 2 with α=s^{-1}, β=b^{-1} gives δ=(b^u)^{-1} and δ^♭=a^u; the counit w∘Q(vV) matches the composite-adjunction definition, and b^u is β^c for the standard compactification as defined in lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility. Step 4 is an elementary coherence check of canonical isomorphisms (flat Tate lines, even shifts). Steps 5–6 set up a correct induction: B_{r+1}^{-1} pastes to A_{r+1} and E_{r+1}=E_r∘F_r(e_u G_r). Step 7: iterating the composition equality and then applying the refinement equality gives β_d∘T(C_A)=C_B T∘B_d on ctf inputs. Step 8: I recomputed the cancellation. Edge cases checked: d=0, K=0, A=B, the nonflat map Z/ℓ²→Z/ℓ, N=1. All six declared tool uses are accepted as generic tools that do not replace the unit route.
